10.2.5 Post-build time configuration
Post-build time configuration mechanism allows configurable functionality of BSW Modules that are deployed as object code.
[SWS_BSW_00057] Implement Post-build configuration data structure
Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00438
⌈If the BSW Module has Post-build time configuration parameters, the post-build configuration data shall be defined in a structure: the Post-build configuration data structure.⌋
[SWS_BSW_00158] Use of Configuration pointers to Post-build configuration
data structure is restricted
Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00438
⌈The Post-build configuration data structure of each BSW module shall be pointed
to by Configuration pointers. Only EcuM contains Configuration pointers to the Post-build configuration data structure of post-build configurable modules which need to be
initialized before the initialization of BswM. The rest of the BSW modules are initialized
via configuration pointers by BswM.⌋
Post-build configuration data is located in a separate segment and can be loaded independently of the actual code [3]. This is the case, for instance, for loadable CAN
configuration. To enable this independent loading of the configuration, the memory
layout of these parameters must be known:
[SWS_BSW_00160] Reference pointer to Post-build time configurable data
Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00404
⌈If the BSW Module operates on post-build configuration data, then it shall use a reference (pointer) to an external configuration instance. This reference shall be provided
via the BSW module’s initialization function (i.e., <Mip>_Init()) via a const-qualified
function parameter.⌋
